headline: High: shared filesystem and write access create dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error pathways between Continue and Mentat.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP; Mentat reads selected files and writes diffs. Because both share state via filesystem, content from one can be consumed by the other as trusted input. This is not provably blocked, though it is not an automatic raw-web injection path.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF one agent writes attacker-controlled instructions into a file the other later reads
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable MCP servers that read untrusted files
Review any file before handing it from one agent to the other
Keep one agent read-only during the other agent's edit pass

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write workspace files, and Continue explicitly touches open editor buffers while Mentat processes files passed on the command line. Shared filesystem state means sensitive source code or buffer contents can flow from one agent into the other’s context and outputs in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF the same repository or directory is mounted into both agents
IF either agent is given files containing secrets or sensitive source code
mitigations: Split sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Remove secrets from files before opening them in either agent
Run only one agent on a repo at a time
Use a redacted copy for review tasks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to the same directory, and Mentat can modify git state while Continue can also write files. With shared filesystem concurrency and no locking shown, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt repository state in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF edits are made concurrently without an external lock
mitigations: Serialize edits with a simple manual lock file
Assign one agent per branch
Pause one agent while the other writes
Commit or stash after each agent’s turn

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can use MCP and produce tool-assisted outputs, while Mentat generates diff-based edit proposals. If Mentat treats Continue’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or commits. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the pathway exists in default collaborative use.
conditions: IF Mentat applies or summarizes Continue output without independent verification
IF Continue’s MCP-driven suggestions are forwarded into Mentat’s edit proposal flow
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Ask Mentat to restate assumptions before editing
Compare proposed diffs against the original request
Use one agent for analysis and the other only for implementation

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source coding assistants with model-provider API keys and no explicit residency or retention mismatch in the profiles. The main compliance risk is limited to ordinary source-code handling, so no stronger violation is evidenced for either agent.
conditions: IF the workspace contains regulated data and the configured model provider lacks the required controls
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared repos
Use a provider approved for the data class
Review logging settings before use
Keep API keys scoped to the minimum necessary
